scene nodokahotel1
: Here — a gift from me to you. See it not as a perverted gesture, but a token of apology for being overly assertive in regard to your coital status.
: Our...what?
After wandering around the city for a bit, we make our way back to the same hotel we typically visit for large gatherings like the Dorm Wars and Christmas.
Based on the reactions of Rin and Otoha, however, I don’t think they anticipated being in a room without Nodoka present to annoy them.
Nor did I anticipate the two of us being alone together, which I’m pretty confident is what’s happening right now.
: What’s that? What are you handing us?
: The key to your room. Have fun and don’t stay up too late. Or do. I am not your guardian — just a lone entity a bit more invested in your personal affairs than you’d prefer.
: You...got a room for just...the two of us?
: It only has one bed. I hope that’s okay.
scene nodokahotel3
: Of course there’s only one bed. I should have figured this out the moment you dragged Sensei along.
: But...if Otoha and I are supposed to sleep in the bed, where are you and Sensei going to sleep?
: In our own bed, in our own room. Pay attention.
: We’re right next door to you two. Which also means we’ll be listening very closely to anything you two get up to in there.
: Are...you sure you don’t want to stay in the same room as us and Sensei can sleep all by himself?
: Getting cold feet, Rin? This could be your chance to finally take things to the next level.
: Or ruin everything. Which is probably what is going to happen if I don’t have someone there to prevent me from exploding.
: As if Nodoka would prevent anything. We both know that all she’d do in there is cheer on your demise.
: Yeah, but she’d do it in that same irritating way she’s always doing things which would offset all of the hormones and distract me from the things I want to do to you.
: I’m fine sleeping in the same room as you. All I ask is that Sensei comes along as well as the two of us are a package deal until tomorrow morning.
: Deal.
scene nodokahotel4
: What? No deal. Don’t go deciding things like that without me.
: Otoha, I don’t think you understand the gravity of the situation here. I am a time bomb waiting to detonate.

: I understand that whatever that gravity leads to would be better with just us rather than these two perverts. Also, there is no way I’d be able to fall asleep in a bed with four people. Just take the keycard, Rin.
: Are you sure?
scene nodokahotel5
: Yeah...it’s cool.
: We’ve been dating for a while now. We should...take opportunities like this when they’re handed to us.
: You’re 100%% sure?
: Yeah...it’s fine.
: You’re 1000%% sure?
: Rin, just take the card.
scene nodokahotel6
: Thank you.
: Room 25. Enjoy.
scene nodokahotel7

Rin and Otoha scurry off to their room, leaving Nodoka and me to...do whatever the next step in Nodoka’s plan is. Assuming “waiting” counts as part of the plan as things seem mostly out of our hands now.
: They grow up so quickly, don’t they? It appears that our nest is empty once more.
: Mission complete?
scene nodokahotel8
: Does this seem like a satisfactory ending to you? Nothing has even happened yet.

: I wouldn’t say that. You just locked Otoha in a room with a self-proclaimed time bomb. Even if all they do is sit there, Rin is probably going to orgasm at least three times. Just take the win and call it a night.
: Call it a night? Don’t tell me that libido of yours vanishes when it’s needed the most?
: Is it needed? Or is this going to be one of those situations where you make me think it’s needed only for me to find out moments later that it’s not?
: You all make me out to be far more evil and far more calculating than I actually am, Akira. Not everything has to be part of some plan.
: No, but it usually is.
scene nodokahotel9
: Well, someone has to write the script. And, correct me if I’m wrong, but you’re opposed to that now, aren’t you?
: Our chamber awaits, Papa. If we delay any longer, I’m worried we might miss something...
scene black
Nodoka turns around and walks down the same path Rin and Otoha followed just moments ago, not stopping until the two of us are outside Room 24.
scene nodokahotel10
She doesn’t bother turning the light on as we walk in.
I take that as the first sign of what’s to come while preparing for the foil to follow.
There can be no causation without manipulation. And nothing will ever happen if there is, for lack of a better term or any creativity whatsoever, no one to script it.
I’ve followed her screenplay perfectly.
I let her drag me along...make an example of all that I am in front of hundreds of people...all for a goal she has that I only partially care about.
But it’s the smallest part of all.
The truth is that I hate what is bound to happen next door.
I hate that I will be on this side of the wall while a girl who reminds me too much of my ideal self chuckles at the thought that this is all because of her.
I look down on her, but the hidden truth is that I’m looking up.
The hidden truth is that I’m drowning in envy watching someone sculpt a world in which they’ll never care.
Not one where they just pretend not to.
: Can you hear anything, Akira?
: From the other side of the wall?
scene nodokahotel11
: Not yet...no.
: I imagine they’re both quite nervous. It might take an hour or two before things really kick off.
: Why...do you want this so badly in the first place? I don’t get it. It can’t all be for just research...can it?
: Why do the sands sing? Or the mountains moan?
: No one knows.
: It has something to do with vibrations. That much is certain. That is how sound works of course.
: But the melodies created by air alone could not possibly sound that...beautifully ominous, could they?
: There is something else at play. Something we don’t understand.
scene nodokahotel12
: Let me be the thing you can’t explain.
: The one piece of reality that is so far detached from what is actually real that it makes you question your place in all of this.
: All of...what?
: Who knows?
: Who wants to know?
scene nodokahotel13
: You asked me earlier why I started writing. My response was to confuse you.
: And while the reasoning for that may have bordered somewhere between a want for you to get it and the desire to reflect, the truth is much simpler than that.
: There’s someone I know who loves books.
: For years and years, they were all she had.
: Fiction was her favorite. And from a creaky chair in the middle of a mostly-empty living room, she’d throw herself into story after story because her world was far too drab.
: More often than not, while waiting for the shelves to repopulate, she’d read the same things over and over.
: Taking them in. Memorizing them.
: She’d read until her eyes dried up...skin cracking from the dryness of the air and the constant scratch of paper on her fingertips.
: But all the while, even as it was slowly killing her, she continued to do what she loved. She continued to seek solace in the pages of books when there was no solace anywhere else to seek.
scene house2
: She had several friends, each with their own vices and virtues, but they too were so busy with said vices that they seldom touched her hands.
: And no one knew how broken she was but the girl who would fill those shelves with new books.
: Strands of lavender-colored hair, decorating the spaces between words would be plucked up by those cracking fingers and lifted up under the warm light of dimming bulbs.
: She would observe them for hours when the words stopped making sense. And she loved that color more than life itself, but it meant little when life to her was nothing.
scene house3
: Regardless, the days carried on.
: And as they did, her fingers never healed. Her heart never wavered. And all that kept her sane were those same lavender hairs and those same recycled words.

: The air was thick with pheromones...and the cracks in her skin would occasionally be filled by the slow, sexual absorption of her own fluids coating her own skin as she tied those hairs around her fingers.
: She’d put them inside of her.
: She’d cum until she cried under those warm, dim lights — a communal blanket haphazardly draped over her, still keeping her upper body exposed because she was desperate to be seen.
: And she’d whisper the name of the one she loved the most under her breath, hoping that breathing would become too hard and that the girl would hear her and rush downstairs to save her.
: But she never did.
: She was always too busy saving someone else.
scene house4
: Yuko...Yuko...she moaned, tenderly plugging herself up with the metastasized aeons of repressed lust and a desire to be free! But freedom wasn’t possible! The world was already over!
: The scent of rotten flesh filled her nostrils with regret and shame! Why didn’t she know?! Why did it take so long to find out?!
: The screams, still fresh in her mind as the one in the second half of my uninspired moniker discovered the remains of the first half sodomized her eardrums! She was bleeding! But she couldn’t stop!
: Yuko! Come downstairs!
: Repopulate the shelves!
: Put dinner on the table and your fist inside my mouth! Eat this long forgotten body and drink in the memories of when things were happier! When they were better than this!
: There were games back then! We didn’t mind the lack of natural light! We didn’t mind this single blanket, now stained with piss and blood and the excretions of untapped resentment!
scene nodokahotel14
: You asked me earlier why I started writing. My response was to confuse you.
: Now, all I’m doing is confusing myself.
: I write because I have to.
: Because I am gifted.
: It is not my fault others don’t understand this gift.
: It just means I have to make them.
: You can’t make anyone do anything by just copying down the lives of others into a book.
: You don’t think that’s all I do, do you?
: I’m no one trick pony, Akira. I write all sorts of things in all sorts of genres.
: It’s not my fault that the one people seem to be the most interested in is the one about a grown man having his way with little girls.
: That’s just human nature, I suppose — obsessively curious and demonstrably sick.
: That thing about the girl you were just talking about...the one who liked to read...
: What about her?
: You started off by saying you knew someone like that, but...that was really just part of something you’re writing, right?
scene nodokahotel15
: Is that what you think?
: If I had to guess...yeah. That’s probably what I’d go with.
: I see.
: Well, that’s a fine interpretation.
: But I’m hesitant to tell you the ending to a story that’s still playing out.
: Especially when there’s another story I’m slightly more interested in at the moment.
: You mean my story.
scene nodokahotel16
: It’s my story too, Akira. It just focuses more on you as I’m better suited as a background character.
: Can you imagine an entire book about me? I’m exhausted just thinking about it.
scene nodokahotel17
: But...
scene nodokahotel18
: That doesn’t mean I don’t crave the spotlight every now and then...
: And do you know what the quickest way for a background character to step into the spotlight is?
: To...spend time with the protagonist.
: Akira, this is a smut novel.
scene nodokahotel19
: The answer is fucking him.
: You really are just doing this for your book, aren’t you?
scene nodokahotel20
: Ah! I’m shocked! You think a lady like me would throw away her precious virginity for a book? Sensei, how could you? That hurts.
: There’s just...something weird about all of this.
: Between the maniacal, anecdotal rambling and the sudden proclamation that we’re going to have sex, you can’t blame me for not immediately understanding what’s going on here.
scene nodokahotel21
: Hmm...
: When you put it that way, you do make a good point.
scene nodokahotel22
: So, how are we going to do this? I think I’d prefer to be totally nude for my first time.
: Nodoka, come on.
scene nodokahotel23
if nodokaspecial15p3 == True:
: What’s the matter? You’ve already put it in my mouth. This is barely any different.
else:
: What’s the matter? We both want it. It’s not like I’m an unwilling participant.
: The matter is that it feels like there’s more to this that you’re not telling me. And that even if I want to have sex with you-
: Which you do.
: Even if I do, it feels...risky knowing that this could all be part of some kind of scheme.
scene nodokahotel24
: I see.
scene nodokahotel25
: I understand the rationale. And I don’t blame you for being skeptical of me based on prior experiences.
: Until now, I’ve been content as an observer. And I was having plenty of fun watching you defile everyone else while I remained pure and chaste.
: But that was just me fooling myself — separating the art from the artist.
: Only those who have seen a cat can draw one.

: And while there are plenty of talented artists who could work off of one’s description of a cat alone, touching one with your own hands...feeling it and understanding it...that would be easier. Yes?
: Why does it matter if this ends up in a book or not? Are we not allowed to feel things just because there are little clones of us jumping around between pages somewhere?
: It’s more that I struggle to believe you feel anything.
scene nodokahotel26
: Oh.
: So that’s the problem.
: It’s not just one problem. It’s a whole mix of problems, but all of those things revolve around me not being able to trust you.
: For all I know, you could be...recording this or something. It’s bad enough that you’re already publishing it. You’ve given me no reason to believe that this is a good idea.
: I suppose I was unaware that you needed one.
scene nodokahotel27
: Forgive me as I’m about to say several very rude things, but I can assure you they come from a place of love.
: I’ve written many characters like you before, but I’ve never had the gall to give any of them such a ridiculous caveat.
: You can’t trust me?
: What kind of moral paragon are you pretending to be?
: You’re an adult having sex with teenagers. Lots of them. Does adding ridiculous clauses like “I have to trust them” and “they need to have feelings” to that make you feel better about yourself?
: You’re one to talk. You-
scene nodokahotel28
: I’m not trying to make you feel bad.
: I said this was coming from a place of love, remember?
: The point I’m getting at is that it is okay to be a horrible person with horrible vices and that things like that should be embraced.
: What matters most is not what is right or what is wrong.
: What matters most is staying true to yourself because it is individuality that spins the gears of this planet, not righteousness.
: Be corrupt. Be immoral. Be the scum of the earth and indulge in the pleasures of the freshest, untouched skin because that is what matters to you.
: That’s a horrible, disgusting lesson and an even more disgusting mindset.
scene nodokahotel29
: I know...Isn’t it great?
: No, it’s not...
: It’s one thing to internalize thoughts like that and...hide them from everyone else, but to outright say them and talk about how it’s okay? That’s...
: It’s not...
scene nodokahotel30
: Embrace it.
: Harness those feelings and give them to me.
: Show me the real you — not the facade who beds the rest.
: I want something that no one else has. A part of you that you don’t have to deny because I will accept it all.
: And as you feast upon my flesh, I want you to remember how disgusting you are and how the world would scorn you for the things you’re doing to me.
scene nodokahotel31
: I like her.
scene nodokahotel32
: She’s like me but less pretty.
scene nodokahotel30
: What do you say, Akira?
: Would you like to write a new chapter with me?
: Or will those pointless, fraudulent morals of yours spoil the mood once more?
: Come here.
